title: Surgical reduction of Console telemetry surface: prune cards, trace sampling, and cost rollup for MVP
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Given tightening timelines and backend ingestion cost constraints, we are trimming the initial Redwood Console telemetry surface to ship an operationally useful MVP. This ticket captures the PRD-level scope cuts, rationale, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and follow-ups. Goal: deliver a small set of high-impact telemetry tiles and a low-cost tracing surface that enables root-cause investigation for high-severity failures while deferring expensive per-token cost attribution and full flamegraph tracing until post-MVP. Rationale and trade-offs: 1) Remove per-request token-level cost attribution (deferred): avoids large ingestion and compute costs; reduces initial engineering scope by ~3 sprints. Trade-off: customers lose fine-grained cost drivers; mitigated by offering aggregated daily cost rollups and route-level deltas. 2) Limit tracing to error-focused sampled traces (deferred: full sampling and spans retention): reduces storage and UI complexity; trade-off: less complete visibility for low-frequency latency regressions. 3) Condense dashboard cards to 3 tier-1 tiles (top routes table, latency percentiles, daily cost rollup) and one diagnostics panel for recent error traces. This provides quick actionable signal for platform SRE and product teams while keeping UI development minimal. 4) Feature gating: advanced cost drilldowns and flamegraph trace view will be gated behind a feature flag and targeted for the next release if cluster costs and ingest stability meet thresholds. Engineering notes: backend will expose a single aggregated cost endpoint per-tenant per-day, latency histograms with 50/95/99 percentiles truncated to 99th bucket, and an error-trace export that samples 1% of requests and 100% of error-producing requests for retention of 7 days. Design notes: proposed compact card designs attached in Design doc. Implementation plan: - Backend contract v1 (aggregated endpoints) implemented behind a feature flag (eng PR linked) - Console UI to render condensed tiles with graceful fallback to 'aggregated only' messaging - Canary rollout to internal Redwood teams + two external beta customers - Metric thresholds and budget caps for ingestion set in Optimize console
acceptance_criteria: UI displays three primary tiles: Top routes table, Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), Daily cost rollup for selected time range
Diagnostics panel surfaces sampled error traces (all error requests + 1% random sample of successful requests) and is filterable by route and time
Console data freshness: aggregated metrics and cost data visible in UI < 120 seconds after ingestion (95th percentile)
Backend ingestion cost for telemetry <= 25% of forecasted budget for Q4 post-launch (ops check), documented in Optimize dashboard
Design review sign-off completed for compact cards (link in 'links')
Engineering review approves API contract and feature-flag gating plan (link to PR), and rollout playbook exists
Canary rollout completed with 3 internal teams and 2 external beta customers with no regression incidents > Sev2
Fallback behavior: when detailed telemetry is disabled or costs exceeded, UI shows clear messaging and a link to enable detailed metrics (admin only)
